stories.title: Sonia Gandhi memoir addresses past leadership tensions
stories.summary: In her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi describes former prime minister P. V. Narasimha Rao as an erudite statesman and recalls the leadership transition involving Sitaram Kesri. She writes that her only disagreement with Rao concerned the pace of the Rajiv Gandhi assassination investigation.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi alleges phone surveillance by Prime Minister
stories.summary: Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi alleged on Friday that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is tapping his phone. Gandhi claims the device contains evidence supporting his allegations against the Prime Minister and has renewed his challenge for a one-on-one debate to determine who is anti-national.

stories.title: Sonia Gandhi criticizes Ayodhya temple inauguration timing
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi writes in her memoir that the Ram Temple consecration ceremony was a hurriedly organized media event held in an incomplete structure. She alleges that Prime Minister Narendra Modi ignored warnings from religious leaders to secure electoral mileage ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

stories.title: Sonia Gandhi recalls origins of Bharat Jodo Yatra
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi writes that the Bharat Jodo Yatra began after Rahul Gandhi observed widespread despondency during the pandemic. She initially attributed his long walks to knee pain, but he later explained he wanted to connect with citizens who felt disillusioned with the current political situation.

stories.title: Sonia Gandhi reflects on Bofors controversy
stories.summary: In her memoir, Sonia Gandhi alleges that the Opposition campaign against Rajiv Gandhi during the Bofors controversy was supported by a corporate house and members of the Congress party. She writes that her husband maintained no agents were involved in the 1987 arms purchase.

stories.title: Sonia Gandhi describes Nitish Kumar's exit from INDIA bloc
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi writes that Nitish Kumar's departure from the INDIA bloc in January 2024 was planned. She recalls him walking out of a meeting after making a feeble excuse before rejoining the BJP-led NDA. The JD(U) has since stated the alliance lacked a clear objective.

stories.title: Sonia book says Nitish Kumar left INDIA bloc meeting after ‘feeble excuse’, JD(U) hits back
stories.summary: The JD(U) has strongly objected to former AICC president Sonia Gandhi writing in her memoir that former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar left the INDIA bloc over “a feeble excuse”. JD(U) national working president Sanjay Kumar Jha said that Kumar was “the chief architect of

stories.title: Differing accounts of 1999 Congress split
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi writes in her memoir that she was moved to tears when Sharad Pawar questioned her eligibility for office due to her foreign birth. In his own 2015 memoir, Pawar provides a different account, stating that Gandhi herself raised the issue for colleague assessment.

stories.title: Sonia Gandhi on Modi's discomfort with elite
stories.summary: In her memoir, Sonia Gandhi writes that she understands Prime Minister Narendra Modi's discomfort with the ruling elite. While critical of his ideology, she notes that his background in an underprivileged world left him feeling ill at ease in Delhi drawing rooms.

stories.title: Bus collision in Assam kills 25
stories.summary: A minibus collided with a container truck in Assam's Golaghat district on Friday, resulting in 25 deaths. The vehicle was carrying over 35 passengers, including students. Several injured survivors remain in critical condition at local hospitals following the head-on crash on National Highway-715.

stories.title: Kaziranga collision kills 25, preliminary probe suggests minibus was ‘speeding’
stories.summary: At least 25 people died on Friday, and several others were injured in a collision that happened near Kaziranga National Park, senior government and police officials said. The head-on collision happened between a minibus and a container truck in the Rangajan area of Golaghat district.

stories.title: At least 25 killed, several injured in road accident in Assam’s Golaghat: Police
stories.summary: At least 25 killed, several injured in road accident in Assam’s Golaghat: Police The passenger vehicle was carrying over 35 people, including students, when it collided head-on with a goods trailer near Rongajan in Golaghat district. Updated on: Nov 13, 2026, 23:00:16 IST By Biswa

stories.title: Survivors report speeding in fatal Assam bus crash
stories.summary: Survivors of the collision in Golaghat claim the minibus was overcrowded and traveling at high speed before swerving into the wrong lane. Dashcam footage from the truck captured the final moments of the crash. Officials confirmed the bus was violating traffic restrictions near the park.

stories.title: ‘Bus was overspeeding, violated restrictions’: Official on Assam accident that killed 25
stories.summary: ‘Bus was overspeeding, violated restrictions’: Official on Assam accident that killed 25 The collision took place at around 2.30 pm when the passenger vehicle was travelling from Bokakhat towards Nagaon and crashed into the goods-carrying vehicle. stories.title: Two train derailments reported in one day
stories.summary: Four coaches of the Chauri Chaura Express derailed near Kanpur Central station on Wednesday evening. Earlier that day, six coaches of the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailed near Digaru station in Assam. No casualties were reported in either incident, according to railway officials.

stories.title: Two missing SPOs found dead in Kishtwar
stories.summary: The bodies of two Special Police Officers, Rashpal Kumar and Bobby Chand, were discovered in Kishtwar on Thursday. Security agencies have identified a local Lashkar-e-Taiba commander as the suspect. The incident marks the first such killing of security personnel in the area since 2000.

stories.title: Two special police officers found dead in Kishtwar
stories.summary: The bodies of two special police officers were recovered from a forest in Kishtwar district on Thursday. The officers went missing while travelling to patrol duty. Officials believe terrorists took their service weapons and ammunition. The incident follows a separate attack on a CRPF checkpost in Kulgam district.

stories.title: CRPF personnel injured in Kulgam terror attack
stories.summary: Three CRPF personnel were injured when suspected terrorists opened fire on a security checkpoint in Kulgam district on Wednesday. The attack occurred while the Lieutenant Governor was inaugurating a festival nearby. This is the third terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir since July.

stories.title: A2B secures $180 million investment from Bodhi Tree
stories.summary: Food chain Adyar Ananda Bhavan has secured $180 million from Bodhi Tree Systems, a firm backed by James Murdoch and Uday Shankar. The deal values the 50-year-old brand at roughly $350 million. The company plans to use the funds to expand into newer markets.

stories.title: WEG to build global manufacturing plant in Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: Brazilian manufacturer WEG will invest approximately ₹2,000 crore to build a global manufacturing facility in Dharmapuri, Tamil Nadu. The project is expected to create 3,000 jobs. The state government aims to spread industrial growth beyond traditional manufacturing hubs.

stories.title: CCPA fines Ola for pre-ride tip feature
stories.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority has fined Ola ₹10 lakh for its pre-ride tip feature. The regulator labeled the tool an unfair trade practice and a dark pattern, directing the company to discontinue it. The feature suggested that extra payments could help passengers secure rides faster.

stories.title: Dubai airport operator suspends SpiceJet check-in services
stories.summary: Dubai Airports has stopped check-in services for SpiceJet over unpaid dues of approximately ₹35.85 crore. The airline has cancelled several flights while stating it is working to resolve the issue. SpiceJet has not specified how it intends to settle the outstanding balance.

stories.title: SpiceJet board to consider fundraising on November 18
stories.summary: SpiceJet has informed the BSE that its board will meet on November 18 to consider raising fresh capital. The airline is exploring options including equity shares, preference shares and debt securities. The carrier continues to face financial difficulties and operational challenges.

stories.title: SpiceJet board to weigh fundraise amid mounting troubles
stories.summary: SpiceJet will meet on November 18 to discuss raising capital as the airline struggles to maintain operations. Company sources claim two investors are interested in the carrier. Whether this results in a change of management remains to be seen.

stories.title: SpiceJet passengers report last-minute flight cancellations
stories.summary: Passengers have reported frequent last-minute cancellations of SpiceJet flights. Travelers cited help desk staff blaming a financial crisis and a shortage of aircraft for the disruptions. The airline has faced ongoing criticism for failing to communicate changes to passengers via email or mobile messaging.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu imposes stock limits on essential food items
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has imposed stock limits on paddy, rice, and pulses to prevent hoarding. Wholesalers, retailers, and millers must clear excess stocks by November 16. The order is intended to curb inflation and manage the high price of essential food items.

stories.title: Centre mandates weekly stock declarations for pulses
stories.summary: The government has made weekly stock declarations mandatory for pulses to prevent artificial price rises. Stockists and retailers must upload data every Friday to a dedicated portal. This follows a similar requirement for rice, as officials attempt to curb hoarding despite comfortable supply levels.

stories.title: Legacy landfill remediation deadline pushed to 2027
stories.summary: The Centre has extended the deadline for clearing legacy landfill sites to December 2027. Despite the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, over 1,000 lakh tonnes of waste remain across 4,632 acres. The mission was originally scheduled to conclude its cleanup efforts by October 2026.

stories.title: CAG audits fertiliser subsidy over urea diversion concerns
stories.summary: The CAG has launched an all-India audit of fertiliser subsidies to investigate the alleged diversion of urea in 169 districts. The government spends over ₹2 lakh crore annually on the subsidy. The audit will assess demand and efficiency, with results expected by mid-2027.

stories.title: BPCL says E20 petrol samples pass quality tests
stories.summary: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited stated that E20 petrol samples tested across 27 states met the required ethanol content range of 19-21%. The company tested 280 samples following concerns raised by a viral photograph of an ethanol separation test. The company maintains its fuel quality is consistent.

stories.title: NITI Aayog flags India's food import dependence
stories.summary: NITI Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri noted that India remains heavily dependent on imports for essential items like edible oils and pulses. He questioned the country's preparedness for global supply disruptions. India currently imports more than half of its edible oil requirements.

stories.title: Cuddalore's Silver Beach receives Blue Flag certification
stories.summary: Silver Beach in Cuddalore has been awarded the Blue Flag certification by the Foundation for Environment Education. The label recognises compliance with criteria regarding water quality, safety, and environmental management. It is one of three beaches in Tamil Nadu to receive the certification for 2026-27.

stories.title: Quad leaders to discuss economic security in Manila
stories.summary: Quad leaders will meet in Manila next week to discuss economic security and strategic infrastructure. The summit marks the first gathering of leaders from India, Australia, Japan and the US since September 2024. The US is set to host the meeting on the margins of the Asean Summit.

stories.title: India and Canada trade talks continue
stories.summary: India and Canada are holding the sixth round of negotiations for a comprehensive economic partnership agreement this week. Both countries aim to resolve outstanding issues and conclude the deal by the end of the year. The talks include provisions for the mobility of professionals between the two nations.

stories.title: Culture minister rejects Pakistan claim to Indus Valley
stories.summary: Culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat stated that Pakistan cannot appropriate the Indus Valley civilisation because the nation is only 80 years old. India is hosting the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi this month to showcase its 5,000-year-old history. Pakistan has not yet responded to the invitation.

stories.title: BrahMos missile exports expand to Southeast Asia
stories.summary: BrahMos Aerospace has supplied missiles to the Philippines and signed an agreement with Vietnam. CEO Jaiteerth R Joshi said several other Southeast Asian nations have expressed interest in the technology. Deals with these countries remain subject to government clearance following a surge in demand for the missile.

stories.title: India ready for bilateral talks with Bangladesh
stories.summary: India stated it is ready to discuss all bilateral issues with Bangladesh, dismissing claims that a consular dialogue was cancelled due to a passport request from former prime minister Sheikh Hasina. The government reiterated its desire for a positive and constructive relationship with the country through existing technical mechanisms.

stories.title: India-Bangladesh consular dialogue to be rescheduled
stories.summary: The fifth round of the India-Bangladesh consular dialogue will be held on a mutually convenient date. The Ministry of External Affairs confirmed the meeting will address travel arrangements and bilateral issues. India maintains it seeks to build forward-looking relations with Bangladesh through its established diplomatic channels.

stories.title: Microsoft services face global disruption
stories.summary: A global outage affecting Microsoft services began Thursday and continued through Friday, impacting email and workplace applications for businesses worldwide. The company reported progress in fixing the disruption, which affected operations from startups to large corporations in India. Microsoft has yet to confirm the cause of the failure.

stories.title: Airlines report communication issues during Microsoft outage
stories.summary: IndiGo and Akasa Air reported disruptions to email support services due to the global Microsoft outage. The airlines advised passengers to use alternative communication channels while monitoring the tech disruption. Air India stated that its own operations and communication systems remained unaffected by the service failure.

stories.title: Microsoft outage follows server restart
stories.summary: Microsoft services including 365, Teams and Outlook experienced a major global outage. The company described the event as a service degradation caused by automated server shutdowns and an infrastructure bottleneck. Engineers have been deploying alternatives, though initial fix attempts did not immediately restore full service stability.

stories.title: Microsoft outage highlights reliance on automated code
stories.summary: A global Microsoft outage lasted several hours on Friday, affecting enterprise and consumer services. The company reported positive results for stability after multiple fix attempts. The incident has raised concerns regarding the speed at which AI agents write code and the ability of engineers to review complex systems.

stories.title: Researchers develop chip to boost 6G speeds
stories.summary: Researchers at the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research have developed a silicon chip for high-frequency signals. The chip allows data transmission at speeds of 100 gigabits per second while maintaining signal strength through compact devices. The team aims to address connectivity challenges for future wireless networks.

stories.title: Airtel chairman calls for higher mobile tariffs
stories.summary: Bharti Airtel founder Sunil Bharti Mittal has called for mobile tariffs to rise to 350 rupees per month. Mittal cited rising operating costs and the need for infrastructure investment. He noted that even at this price, India would continue to have some of the cheapest mobile tariffs globally.

stories.summary: India's ethanol capacity can boost SAF production, but policy gaps a hurdle: AIDA's Bharati Balaji | HT interview In an interview with Hindustan Times, Bharati Balaji said that not feedstock availability but policy is the biggest challenge. stories.title: Regulator warns on anti-cancer drug prices
stories.summary: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority has warned of penal action against those failing to comply with price caps on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs. The authority ordered companies to prominently display updated price lists. State drug controllers must submit action taken reports by November 16.

stories.title: NPPA mandates price display for cancer drugs
stories.summary: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority has directed all manufacturers, retailers and hospitals to prominently display revised prices for 137 anti-cancer drugs. The trade margin rationalisation policy took effect on November 9. The regulator has called for strict monitoring to ensure compliance across all medical premises and websites.

stories.title: Patent filings for HIV drug face opposition
stories.summary: Eighteen patent applications for the HIV drug lenacapavir have been filed in India, raising concerns over market exclusivity and access to affordable generics. Patient groups have filed oppositions, arguing the applications lack novelty. The drug is designated as essential by the World Health Organization for HIV prevention and treatment.

stories.title: Row erupts over foreign medicos' MD Physician title
stories.summary: A dispute has emerged regarding the MD Physician title used by foreign medical graduates in India. While the title denotes a primary degree abroad, critics argue it is being confused with Indian postgraduate qualifications. Doctors warn of patient confusion, while graduates maintain their credentials are officially recognised.

stories.title: NMC seeks report on Banswara medical college allegations
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission has directed Government Medical College, Banswara, to investigate allegations of ragging and sexual assault involving first-year MBBS students. The institution must submit a detailed action-taken report within 24 hours of the notice issued by the commission's Anti-Ragging Cell on Wednesday.

stories.title: Illegal oocyte extraction racket uncovered in Hyderabad
stories.summary: Police in Telangana rescued 43 women from an illegal oocyte extraction and commercial sale racket following raids on October 30. One victim reported being lured into the scheme to pay off debts incurred by her father's kidney failure. The full investigation details are for subscribers.

stories.title: Thalassemia patients receive pension sanction orders
stories.summary: Children affected by thalassemia met with Revenue and Housing Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy to acknowledge the sanction of pensions under the Cheyutha Scheme. The Minister distributed orders to 1,138 eligible beneficiaries, following advocacy efforts regarding the welfare of those living with the condition in the state.

stories.title: Chennai Airport hosts walkathon for diabetes awareness
stories.summary: Kauvery Hospital and the Airports Authority of India hosted a walkathon at Chennai Airport to promote physical activity for diabetes management. The event featured medical professionals and local officials, highlighting the importance of lifestyle choices in preventing and managing the condition ahead of World Diabetes Day.

stories.title: CMC Vellore to host diabetes awareness event
stories.summary: Christian Medical College, Vellore, will hold an exhibition and poster competition on November 13 to mark World Diabetes Day. The event, themed around early action, aims to increase public awareness regarding diabetes prevention and holistic management. Free blood glucose screenings will be available to attendees.

stories.title: Six scholars awarded Infosys Prize 2026
stories.summary: The Infosys Science Foundation has announced six winners for the 2026 Infosys Prize. Recipients include scholars in fields ranging from quantum physics to constitutional law. Gautam Bhatia was recognised in the Humanities and Social Sciences category for legal scholarship that integrates sociology, political theory and moral philosophy.

stories.title: Rajya Sabha panel reviews HAL and ISRO facilities
stories.summary: A Rajya Sabha committee led by Milind Deora visited Bengaluru to inspect defence and space institutions. The group toured Hindustan Aeronautics Limited facilities and reviewed the implementation of corporate social responsibility rules. The visit provided an opportunity to showcase contributions to indigenous aerospace development and defence platforms.

stories.title: Bay of Bengal low-pressure area to intensify
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department reports that a low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by the evening of November 16. The system formed under the influence of an upper-air circulation over the central Andaman Sea.

stories.title: Low-pressure system forms over Bay of Bengal
stories.summary: A low-pressure area formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal on Friday morning. The India Meteorological Department expects the system to move northwestwards and intensify into a depression by November 15. The weather agency is currently monitoring the circulation over the central Andaman Sea.

stories.title: Bay of Bengal system likely to become cyclonic storm
stories.summary: A low-pressure area formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal on Friday and is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by November 16. The Cyclone Warning Centre predicts the system will move northwestwards, becoming a well-marked low-pressure area before developing into a depression on Sunday.

stories.title: Man killed by explosive device hidden in sweet
stories.summary: A 35-year-old man in Madhya Pradesh died after a crude explosive device, allegedly intended for killing wild boars, was concealed inside a rasgulla and detonated in his mouth. Police have arrested a fellow villager in connection with the incident, which occurred during a family gathering.

stories.title: Two arrested after fatal explosive incident in MP
stories.summary: Two men have been arrested following the death of a 35-year-old man in Dindori district. The victim died after biting into a rasgulla that contained a concealed crude bomb. Police report the device was presented to the man while he was sitting with his family.

stories.title: Political rivals meet at memorial ritual
stories.summary: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor held a brief, cordial meeting during a memorial ritual for the late BJP leader RK Sinha. The encounter, involving a handshake and a smile, occurred during the final-day rites held on October 30.

stories.title: Ethereum founder attends Mumbai blockchain event
stories.summary: Vitalik Buterin, cofounder of Ethereum, attended the eighth edition of Devcon in Mumbai. The event drew approximately 5,000 attendees to the city. While the blockchain community gathered for the conference, the scale of the event remained largely unnoticed by the general public.

stories.title: BJP MP apologises for remarks on farmers
stories.summary: BJP MP Janardan Mishra has issued an apology following public backlash over comments suggesting farmers spend nine months of the year playing cards and drinking. The MP stated he had no intention of insulting the farming community and claimed his remarks were distorted during a local programme.
